nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued function of two real variables whose graph is doubly ruled; no continuity of $f$ is assumed. Then there are real numbers $a, b, c, d, e, g$ such that $f(x, y) = ax^2 + bxy + cy^2 + dx + ey + g$ for all real $x$ and $y$, and either $a = b = c = 0$ (the graph is a plane) or $b^2 - 4ac > 0$ (the graph is a hyperbolic paraboloid).
nodes.title: Doubly ruled graphs are planes or hyperbolic paraboloids

nodes.summary: The graph of a real-valued function $f$ of two real variables is doubly ruled when for every point $(x_0, y_0) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ there are $(u_1, v_1, w_1)$ and $(u_2, v_2, w_2)$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ such that the lines through $(x_0, y_0, f(x_0, y_0))$ with directions $(u_1, v_1, w_1)$ and $(u_2, v_2, w_2)$ both lie in the graph of $f$, and $(u_2, v_2)$ is not a real multiple of $(u_1, v_1)$.
nodes.title: Doubly ruled graph

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued function of two real variables, and let $x_0, y_0, u, v, w$ be real numbers. The line through $(x_0, y_0, f(x_0, y_0))$ with direction $(u, v, w)$ lies in the graph of $f$ when $(u, v) \ne (0, 0)$ and $f(x_0 + tu, y_0 + tv) = f(x_0, y_0) + tw$ for every real $t$.
nodes.title: Line lying in a graph
